rubric_100.why_external_matters: The 78-point V3 version was anchored by public-value passport, rights, reversibility, and civic benefit logic.
External score declined when source/data/depth/metric anchors were compressed from V3 levels.
V3 explicitly compared routes and justified the chosen public-value commons model.
AI scoring appears to reward auditable decision rules, evidence levels, gates, rollback, and non-digital fallback more than visual AI symbolism.
V6 improved drawings, but the gain was not enough without hard spatial parameters; this dimension should be weighted below protocol/evidence until metrics are hardened.
Scores need actors, phases, cost bands, ownership gaps, and failure exits rather than only staging diagrams.
All accepted versions passed compliance; this is a gate and guardrail, not a high-score substitute.
Packaging is necessary for intake, but V6 shows packaging alone does not raise the external score.

calibration_rule: Do not claim 90+ internally unless the package both restores V3-level public-value/evidence structure and adds hard spatial/implementation parameters that are visible in drawings and machine-readable assets. Treat deterministic CI/self-check as gate readiness, not content score.
